---
title: "Systematic benchmarking of tools"
format: html
---

These pages compare analysis tools on the simulated MAD^4^HatTeR datasets. How those datasets were made is described in [Simulated datasets](data_simulated.qmd).

Each comparison keeps one parameter set per tool: the set with the highest Lin's concordance. For sample-level COI, that concordance is calculated on samples whose true COI is 2 through 9. The rule is applied separately on the full panel and on the 15-target panel.

Checking convergence is important for tools that use Markov chain Monte Carlo ([MOIRE](../tutorials/moire/moire_background.Rmd), [TheREALMcCOIL](../tutorials/THEREALMcCOIL/RMCL_background.Rmd), and [FreqEstimationModel](../tutorials/FreqEstimationModel/background.Rmd)). Summaries of convergence are on the individual tool benchmarking pages and are not used to change the chosen set.

The comparisons keep four simulation regimes. Populations with no cotransmission are left out, as are low mean COI with high cotransmission and high mean COI with low cotransmission.

- [Sample-level COI](../benchmarking/coi_sample.qmd)
- [Population mean COI](../benchmarking/coi_mean.qmd)
- [Effective COI](../benchmarking/moire_ecoi.qmd)
- [Single-locus variant frequency](../benchmarking/freq_single_locus_variant.qmd)
- [Single-locus microhaplotype frequency](../benchmarking/freq_single_microhaplotype.qmd)
- [Multi-locus variant frequency](../benchmarking/freq_multi_locus_variant.qmd)
